title: MCP servers
description: The 7 read-only MCP servers at https://mcp.staffops.space/<name> (kubernetes, grafana, argocd, dependency-track, keycloak, prometheus, kubectl; plus Tempo's built-in /tempo) behind Gateway mcp with Keycloak JWT: per-server request rate / status codes / latency from the Gateway's Envoy (Istio standard metrics), pod health and resources for all 7, and the own metrics of the three servers that export them (kubernetes-mcp, grafana-mcp, prometheus-mcp). No official dashboard exists for any of them. Docs: docs/dashboards/ai.md.

panels.title: How to read this dashboard
panels.description: How to read this dashboard.

options.content:
**What it is.** AI assistants reach the lab through **MCP servers** at `https://mcp.staffops.space/<name>`. The dedicated
Gateway **`mcp`** (Istio, `192.168.68.241`) checks a **Keycloak JWT** (groups `/mcp/admin`, `/mcp/viewer`), strips it and
routes by path to the server in namespace `mcp-servers`. Every server is **read-only**.

| Path | Server | Own metrics |
|---|---|---|
| /kubernetes | kubernetes-mcp-server | yes (`k8s_mcp_*`) |
| /grafana | mcp-grafana | yes (`mcp_server_operation_*`, `http_*`) |
| /prometheus | prometheus-mcp-server | yes (`prom_mcp_*`) |
| /argocd, /dependency-track, /keycloak, /kubectl | — | no (Gateway + pod metrics only) |
| /tempo | Tempo built-in (namespace monitoring) | Gateway only |

**Healthy looks like:** all 7 deployments UP, Gateway responses 2xx/202 (MCP notifications answer 202), no 5xx, tool
calls answered in seconds. **401** = no/expired Keycloak token, **403** = token without an allowed group — both are
rejections by the Gateway, not server faults.

**When something goes red:** a server DOWN → `kubectl --context k8s01 -n mcp-servers describe pod -l app=<name>` (most
start failures are a missing key in Vault `homelab/mcp` → CreateContainerConfigError); 5xx for one path → that server's
logs in Loki; many 401/403 → client token / Keycloak (Security dashboards).

panels.title: Deployments available
panels.description: kube_deployment_status_replicas_available per Deployment in mcp-servers (kube-state-metrics). 1 = serving, 0 = that path answers 503 at the Gateway. Same signal as the mixin alert KubeDeploymentReplicasMismatch (https://github.com/kubernetes-monitoring/kubernetes-mixin).

panels.title: Gateway requests/s
panels.description: All requests routed by Gateway mcp to a backend (istio_requests_total from the Gateway Envoy, reporter=source; Istio Service dashboard formula, https://github.com/istio/istio/tree/master/manifests/addons/dashboards (Istio Service/Workload dashboards)).

panels.title: Gateway 5xx ratio (range)
panels.description: Share of requests answered 5xx over the range: 1 - (non-5xx / all), the Istio dashboards' 'success rate' (response_code !~ "5.*") inverted (https://github.com/istio/istio/tree/master/manifests/addons/dashboards (Istio Service/Workload dashboards)). 5xx = backend down, crashed or failing. Thresholds: any 5xx yellow, >5 % red.

targets.expr: (sum(increase(istio_requests_total{reporter="source", source_workload="mcp-istio", source_workload_namespace="gateway", response_code=~"5.."}[$__range])) or vector(0)) / sum(increase(istio_requests_total{reporter="source", source_workload="mcp-istio", source_workload_namespace="gateway"}[$__range]))

panels.title: Auth rejections (range)
panels.description: Requests answered 401 (no/invalid Keycloak JWT) or 403 (JWT without group /mcp/admin or /mcp/viewer) over the range, from istio_requests_total response_code. A few = a client with an expired token; a steady flow = misconfigured client or probing.

panels.title: Restarts (range)
panels.description: increase(kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total) over the range for all MCP pods (kube-state-metrics; KubePodCrashLooping signal).

panels.title: Requests/s by server
panels.description: sum by (destination_service_name) of rate(istio_requests_total) from the Envoy of Gateway mcp (Istio Service dashboard formula, https://github.com/istio/istio/tree/master/manifests/addons/dashboards (Istio Service/Workload dashboards)). Each path maps to one Service (tempo = Tempo's built-in MCP). Series appear only after a server got its first request since the gateway pod started.

panels.title: Non-2xx responses by server and code
panels.description: rate(istio_requests_total) for response codes other than 2xx, per server and code. 401/403 = rejected by the Gateway's JWT policy; 307 = redirect (keycloak-mcp answers /mcp → /mcp/); 404 = unknown path; 5xx = server problem. Empty = every response was 2xx in the window.

targets.expr: sum by (destination_service_name, response_code) (rate(istio_requests_total{reporter="source", source_workload="mcp-istio", source_workload_namespace="gateway", response_code!~"2.."}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: p95 request duration by server
panels.description: histogram_quantile(0.95) of istio_request_duration_milliseconds_bucket per server (Istio Service dashboard formula). For MCP over streamable HTTP, POST /mcp requests last as long as the tool call; a GET that opens an event stream lasts until the client disconnects, which shows up as very long outliers. Empty for a server without requests in the window.

panels.title: Requests in range by server and status
panels.description: increase(istio_requests_total[$__range]) per server and response code: who is used, who fails, who is rejected.

panels.title: CPU by pod (cores)
panels.description: node_namespace_pod_container:container_cpu_usage_seconds_total:sum_irate by pod — the recording rule used by the kubernetes-mixin k8s-resources-namespace dashboard (https://github.com/kubernetes-monitoring/kubernetes-mixin). MCP servers idle near 0; spikes line up with tool calls.

panels.title: Memory working set by pod
panels.description: container_memory_working_set_bytes by pod (kubernetes-mixin k8s-resources-namespace formula). The working set is what the kubelet compares with the limit for OOM kills.

targets.expr: sum by (pod) (container_memory_working_set_bytes{job="kubelet", metrics_path="/metrics/cadvisor", namespace="mcp-servers", container!="", image!=""})

panels.title: Memory working set / limit
panels.description: Working set divided by the memory limit per container (kubernetes-mixin k8s-resources-namespace 'Memory Usage (WSS) / Limits' column). Thresholds: yellow 80 %, red 90 % — near 100 % the container is OOM-killed.

targets.expr: sum by (container) (container_memory_working_set_bytes{job="kubelet", metrics_path="/metrics/cadvisor", namespace="mcp-servers", container!="", image!=""}) / sum by (container) (kube_pod_container_resource_limits{namespace="mcp-servers", resource="memory"})

panels.title: Containers not running (waiting reason)
panels.description: kube_pod_container_status_waiting_reason == 1 (kube-state-metrics; mixin alert KubeContainerWaiting). Lists containers stuck in CreateContainerConfigError (missing Secret key, e.g. Vault homelab/mcp), ImagePullBackOff, CrashLoopBackOff… Empty = every container is running (healthy).

panels.title: Tool calls/s by tool
panels.description: rate(k8s_mcp_tool_calls_total) by tool_name (https://github.com/containers/kubernetes-mcp-server/blob/main/docs/OTEL.md#prometheus-metrics). MCP protocol methods (initialize, tools/list) are counted too; real tools appear as their name (resources_list, pods_log, …). Counters are created on the first call after a pod start; until then the fallback shows 0 (pattern from dashboard 14574).

panels.title: Tool errors/s by tool
panels.description: rate(k8s_mcp_tool_errors_total) by tool_name (https://github.com/containers/kubernetes-mcp-server/blob/main/docs/OTEL.md#prometheus-metrics). The counter is created on the first error, so 'no errors yet' shows as 0 (the 'or up*0' fallback follows the pattern of the official nvidia dashboard 14574). Errors are usually RBAC denials (the server has the view role, no Secrets) or missing resources.

panels.title: p95 tool duration
panels.description: histogram_quantile(0.95) of k8s_mcp_tool_duration_seconds_bucket by tool_name (https://github.com/containers/kubernetes-mcp-server/blob/main/docs/OTEL.md#prometheus-metrics). Slow calls = large list/log responses or a slow API server.

panels.title: HTTP requests/s by path and status class
panels.description: rate(k8s_mcp_http_requests_total) by url_path and http_response_status_class (https://github.com/containers/kubernetes-mcp-server/blob/main/docs/OTEL.md#prometheus-metrics). /mcp is the MCP endpoint, /healthz the probes, /metrics the scrape; 4xx on /mcp = rejected requests (e.g. Host check, bad session).

panels.title: Requests in flight by MCP method
panels.description: k8s_mcp_requests_in_flight by mcp_method_name (https://github.com/containers/kubernetes-mcp-server/blob/main/docs/OTEL.md#prometheus-metrics): requests being handled right now. A tools/call that stays > 0 for long = a stuck call. The gauge appears with the first request after a pod start (0 before).

panels.title: MCP operations/s by method and tool
panels.description: rate of mcp_server_operation_duration_seconds_count by mcp_method_name and gen_ai_tool_name — OpenTelemetry MCP semantic conventions, documented in https://github.com/grafana/mcp-grafana/blob/main/docs/sources/developer/observability-metrics-and-tracing.md.

panels.title: Failed operations/s by tool and error type
panels.description: Operations that carry the error_type label (OTel semconv: set only when the operation failed; https://github.com/grafana/mcp-grafana/blob/main/docs/sources/developer/observability-metrics-and-tracing.md). 0 = no failures since the pod started (fallback 'or up*0' as in dashboard 14574).

targets.expr: sum by (gen_ai_tool_name, error_type) (rate(mcp_server_operation_duration_seconds_count{job="grafana-mcp", error_type!=""}[$__rate_interval])) or on () (sum(up{job="grafana-mcp"}) * 0)

panels.title: p95 operation duration by tool
panels.description: histogram_quantile(0.95) of mcp_server_operation_duration_seconds_bucket by gen_ai_tool_name (https://github.com/grafana/mcp-grafana/blob/main/docs/sources/developer/observability-metrics-and-tracing.md). Includes the time Grafana/datasources take to answer queries the tool runs.

panels.title: Calls to the Grafana API by status
panels.description: rate of http_client_request_duration_seconds_count by http_response_status_code (otelhttp client instrumentation, OTel HTTP semconv). grafana-mcp calls http://grafana.monitoring with a service-account token (Vault homelab/mcp: grafana-token): 401/403 here = token revoked or missing permissions.

panels.title: p95 latency: MCP HTTP server vs Grafana API
panels.description: histogram_quantile(0.95) of http_server_request_duration_seconds_bucket (requests into grafana-mcp, documented in https://github.com/grafana/mcp-grafana/blob/main/docs/sources/developer/observability-metrics-and-tracing.md) and of http_client_request_duration_seconds_bucket (its calls to Grafana). If both rise together, Grafana is the slow part.

panels.title: Server ready
panels.description: prom_mcp_server_ready: 1 when the server is ready (same state as its readiness probe, https://github.com/tjhop/prometheus-mcp-server#metrics).

panels.title: Tool calls/s and failures
panels.description: rate of prom_mcp_tool_call_duration_seconds_count by tool_name, and rate(prom_mcp_tool_calls_failed_total) (https://github.com/tjhop/prometheus-mcp-server#metrics; failures exclude calls cancelled by the client), plus rate(prom_mcp_api_calls_failed_total) by target_path (failed calls to the Prometheus HTTP API). The failure counters appear on the first failure; until then the fallback shows 0. Counter appears on the first failure; until then the fallback shows 0.

panels.title: p95 duration: tools vs Prometheus API
panels.description: histogram_quantile(0.95) of prom_mcp_tool_call_duration_seconds_bucket by tool_name and of prom_mcp_api_call_duration_seconds_bucket by target_path (https://github.com/tjhop/prometheus-mcp-server#metrics). When tool time ≈ API time, Prometheus is the slow part (heavy PromQL).
